items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — went straight from greeting into the customer's question with no roadmap for the call
Never asked 'how are you today?' — customer opened with 'good morning' and Jack didn't reciprocate
Name was guessed off the file ('is it Mike, Michael, El') and then never used again for the rest of the call
No 'pricing is super simple' opener before quoting $204/hr
Never stated crew size or truck count — customer heard '$204 an hour' with no idea how many movers that buys
Never explained what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools)
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — customer explicitly opened the door with 'I saw what you... which is nice about protecting the furniture'
No insurance explanation at all (No Worries + 60c/lb baseline)
Meet Your Mover not pitched
On-Time Guarantee not pitched — a real miss on a call whose entire subject was arrival timing at a building with a 12-9pm delivery window
No 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, transportation fees, fuel surcharge, assembly fees)
No deposit required never mentioned
Packing services never offered or priced
Probe was thin: no box count, no garage/storage/balcony, no additional stops, no storage stops, no parking/COI/elevator access at either address, no long-walk or hallway questions
Never asked about moving stressors — customer was visibly anxious about the property's rules and Jack never named that
Walk distance never discussed despite a third-floor walk-up on the destination side
No school-bus or other equivalents used to frame the estimate
No sense-check after the clock explanation and no 'does that make sense?' close after the prep speech
Email handoff was one clause ('send you a new little email here') — no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' and no hours / how-to-reach-us before hanging up
Said 'the fifth floor and then again the third floor' — a factual stumble on the single biggest time driver in the estimate
top_strength: Jack answered the customer's real question before anything else and answered it with math, not reassurance — walking through load time to show that a morning start still lands the unload at 12:30-1:00, inside the building's 12-9pm window. He then delivered a genuine Save Your Ass prep speech (box everything, take the hanging clothes and artwork in your car, boxes-and-furniture moves fastest) and adjusted the software's 6-hour autobooking estimate up to 6-7 hours for the third-floor walk-up.
coaching_note: This call had a wide-open door for the differentiators and Jack walked past it twice. The customer's entire reason for calling was arrival timing at a building with a 12-9pm delivery window — that is the On-Time Guarantee pitch handed to him on a plate. Then the customer said out loud that the furniture protection 'is nice,' which is the No Worries Damage Coverage + 60c/lb explanation handed to him a second time. He answered neither. Add to that: he quoted $204/hr without ever saying how many movers that buys. Coach Jack to treat post-booking confirmation calls as full sales calls — customer question first (he does this well), then rate WITH crew size, what's included, No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, no hidden fees — and to close with 'any other questions before I let you go?' instead of the abrupt 'thank you so much, sir, bye-bye.'
phone_presence_notes: Easygoing and efficient with some light warmth ('Cool,' 'no worries,' 'Easy'), but he never used the customer's name once after guessing it, didn't acknowledge the customer's stress about the property's rules, and ended the call abruptly.
